newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Ten killed in Somali ambush.
newsitem.headline: Ten killed in Somali ambush.

text.p: Ten people were killed and six wounded when unidentified gunmen ambushed a truck 60 km (40 miles) south of Mogadishu, witnesses reported.
They said the truck, carrying goods and passengers, was attacked while heading for Baidoa town on Saturday. The truck overturned as the driver tried to escape from the ambush by driving off the road.
Among the dead were a mother and her three children aged between one and eight years.
The attack came only two days after leaders of the two main Somali factions announced agreement to end hostilities and work for reconciliation in the war-torn country.
Ali Mohammed Mahdi and Hussein Farah Aideed, respective leaders of the Somali Salvation Alliance and the United Somali Congress, announced their agreement after two days of talks in Cairo.
They said they had agreed to halt all hostilities among the Somalis and to work to convene a summit for national reconciliation within the next few months.

Somalia has been without an effective government since January 1991 when the Mogadishu government of dictator Mohamed Siad Barre was overthrown. The south of the country has since been controlled by a number of different armed factions, while the north has declared its secession and independence as the Republic of Somaliland, with its capital in Hargeisa.
